title: Margaret Hamilton, who sent Apollo 11 to the moon, dies at 90
title_zh: 让阿波罗11号登月的玛格丽特·汉密尔顿去世，享年90岁

image.credit: Photo by Keith Luke on Unsplash
image.author: Keith Luke

lead: Margaret Hamilton wrote the software for the Apollo 11 moon landing. She died at 90. MIT shared the news on Wednesday.
lead_zh: 玛格丽特·汉密尔顿为阿波罗11号登月编写了软件。她去世了，享年90岁。麻省理工学院在周三公布了这一消息。

paragraphs: Hamilton worked at MIT as a computer scientist. In 1969, she led the team that wrote software for Apollo 11. She was the first programmer to join the project.
Minutes before the landing, an alarm rang on the spacecraft computer. The software fixed the problem by itself. The mission continued and the landing was a success.

body:
Hamilton worked at MIT as a computer scientist. In 1969, she led the team that wrote software for Apollo 11. She was the first programmer to join the project.

Minutes before the landing, an alarm rang on the spacecraft computer. The software fixed the problem by itself. The mission continued and the landing was a success.

In 2016, Barack Obama gave her the Presidential Medal of Freedom. He said the astronauts had Margaret Hamilton to thank. She is survived by her family.

body_original:
Margaret Hamilton, trailblazer whose software powered Apollo 11 moon landing, dies aged 90
MIT computer scientist led development of software for moon mission and earned Presidential Medal of Freedom
Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
announced
on Wednesday. She was 90.
In an era before titles such as software engineer and computer scientist became mainstream, Hamilton, who died on 30 September, learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist.
She continued to perfect the craft in an MIT laboratory, writing software that could detect enemy aircraft. When the institute received a Nasa contract to develop the Apollo onboard flight software, she jumped at the opportunity.
“I was attracted both by the sheer idea and the fact that it had never been done before. I was the first programmer to join and the first woman they hired,” she
told
the Guardian in 2019.
In 1969, minutes before the
Apollo 11
spacecraft was set to make history by landing on the lunar surface, an onboard computer’s alarm rang, indicating an emergency.
Faced with a decision of whether to abort the mission, the spacecraft continued on. The software was working just as Hamilton and her team intended.
“It quickly became clear the software was not only informing everyone that there was a hardware-related problem but was compensating for it – restarting and re-establishing the highest priority tasks. The error detection and recovery mechanisms had come to the rescue,” Hamilton said.
Barack Obama referenced the incident when he presented her with the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016.
“Our astronauts didn’t have much time, but thankfully they had Margaret Hamilton,” he said.
Hamilton is survived by her daughter, a son-in-law, two grandsons and four great-grandchildren,
according
to MIT.
Reflecting on the mission, in a 2009
interview
with MIT News, Hamilton said: “Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world; there was no choice but to be pioneers; no time to be beginners.”
